candidate.answerReason: The distinct meeting times, measured from the initial observation, are 200, 240, 260, 280, and 320 seconds. Meetings at a truck arrival or departure are counted only once.

methods.label: Count meetings during drives and stops
methods.explanation:
The truck takes \(200/10=20\) seconds to drive between consecutive pails, followed by a \(30\)-second stop. Its motion therefore repeats in \(50\)-second cycles. Count meetings separately during the driving and stopped portions, then remove any repeated endpoint times.

Let \(t=0\) be the initial observation, and measure position from Michael's initial pail. Michael's position is \(5t\), while the truck starts at position \(200\). Number the truck's subsequent drives by integers \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\). Drive \(k\) starts at time \(50k\), at position \(200(k+1)\), and ends at time \(50k+20\).

During that drive, equality of positions requires
\[
5t=200(k+1)+10(t-50k),
\]
which gives \(t=60k-40\). This time belongs to the drive precisely when
\[
50k\le60k-40\le50k+20,
\]
or \(4\le k\le6\). Thus driving meetings occur at \(t=200,260,320\).

After drive \(k\), the truck is stopped at position \(200(k+2)\) from time \(50k+20\) through \(50k+50\). A meeting then requires
\[
5t=200(k+2),\qquad t=40k+80.
\]
The time lies in this stop exactly when
\[
50k+20\le40k+80\le50k+50,
\]
which gives \(3\le k\le6\). These meetings occur at \(t=200,240,280,320\).

The drive and stop intervals cover all future times. The times \(200\) and \(320\) appear in both lists because they are transition times, so each counts once. The complete list of distinct meetings is
\[
200,\ 240,\ 260,\ 280,\ 320.
\]
They meet \(\boxed{5}\) times, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
